stage_strategy_draft.description: Write a proposed change into the player's draft of one strategy, so it lands in their strategy editor as an attributed unsaved change. This does NOT commit: nothing reaches the live strategy until commit_strategy_draft. Read the draft with get_strategy_draft first, propose against what it shows, and name the draftVersion that read returned (0 when there was no draft). Omit strategyId to open a NEW create draft for a strategy that does not exist yet; the response carries the id minted for it, which every later call names. Axes: IDENTITY — { name, description, tagline }; the name is trimmed, and a new strategy requires it; TIMEFRAME_PROFILE — { timeframe }, the main candle; a new strategy requires it; REPORT — { sections }, the ordered report; a new strategy without it starts from the platform's starting report; MARKET_READ — { marketReadText }; CONDITIONS — { conditions }, each with its verdict, hold and exit flag; the only deterministic entry gate — with no required and no verdict-carrying entry condition the strategy never routes and never enters the arena, and the draft warns NO_ENTRY_CONDITION; ENTRY — { entry }: { trigger: "ON_CANDLE_CLOSE" } alone, or a level trigger with levelOffsetAtrMultiple and validForBars; TRADE_LEVEL_POLICY — { minStopLossAtrMultiple, maxStopLossAtrMultiple, minRiskRewardRatio, minAtrPct }, minAtrPct the ATR% volatility floor a coin must clear; POSITION_MANAGEMENT — all thirteen exit-policy fields. Each axis you send is written WHOLE; axes you omit keep their values. The axes one call sends may serialise to at most 256,000 UTF-8 bytes; a larger stage is refused with VALIDATION_ERROR on axes, and nothing is written. Values are checked for structure here and judged in whole by the diagnostics this call returns — the refusals the commit would raise, and observations that never refuse — so read them and stage again until there are no errors. Refused with DRAFT_AXIS_CONTESTED, naming the axes, when the player's own hand changed one of them after the version you name, and with DRAFT_VERSION_MOVED when that version is one the draft never reached — read from a draft since committed or discarded: read again and propose against what the player now has.

strategyId.description: The strategy whose draft to stage into. Omit it to open a NEW create draft; the response carries the id minted for it, which every later call names.

draftVersion.description: The draft version this proposal was made against: the `draftVersion` get_strategy_draft returned, or 0 when it found no draft (and for a new create draft).

axes.description: The proposed axes, each written WHOLE. Axes you omit keep the values the draft has.

metricKey.description: A metric key list_strategy_vocabulary serves; search it with `query`.

get_strategy_draft.description: Read the player's draft of one strategy with everything a commit needs: the draft (null when the player holds none), its draftVersion (0 when there is none), the committedRevision it would be published over (null for a strategy not created yet), a diff of every drafted axis against the live strategy with the fields that differ, the diagnostics the commit would refuse or observe, and the impact of committing it. A draftVersion names one state of the draft: every write to it — a stage, an edit in the player's editor, a status change re-basing it, a commit clearing the axes it published — moves it, so a version is good until the next write. Read this before staging and again before committing: another of the player's surfaces can change the draft while you work. Show the player the diff and the impact, and commit only on their explicit word.

commit_strategy_draft.description: Publish the player's draft of one strategy. Name the draftVersion and, as expectedRevision, the committedRevision get_strategy_draft returned (null for a strategy not created yet): the commit publishes exactly that draft over exactly that revision, through the same commit the strategy editor's Save runs, and clears the axes it published from the draft. Committed edits take effect on every agent bound to the strategy immediately, and the commit closes no position. An open position never gates or refuses the commit: it keeps the exit rules, exit policy and levels it opened with, so those edits reach only positions opened after the commit. Commit only after the player has seen the diff and the impact and explicitly confirmed. Refused with DRAFT_VERSION_MOVED when the draft changed after your read and CONFLICT when the strategy did — read again and show the player what it now holds — and with the validation error the diagnostics named when the draft cannot be committed — stage a fix. Each such refusal carries nextAct: get_draft or stage. A retry of the same draftVersion returns the first commit's receipt.

expectedRevision.description: The `committedRevision` get_strategy_draft returned: null for a strategy not created yet.

list_strategy_drafts.description: Answer 'what am I part-way through?' for strategys: one page of the player's drafts, newest first, each with its strategy (or none yet, for a create draft), when it was last touched, which surface touched it and whether its base revision has moved. Call this before starting a new strategy and offer to continue a draft rather than starting a second one beside it. Paginate with the returned cursor.

cursor.description: The nextCursor a previous page returned; omit for the first page.

window.description: Trailing window ending now, over the instant the list is ordered by. LIFETIME (the default) is no trailing window, and is the only value that takes since / until.

since.description: Inclusive lower bound (ISO-8601 with offset) on the instant the list is ordered by; omit for no lower bound. Only with window LIFETIME.

until.description: Exclusive upper bound (ISO-8601 with offset) on the instant the list is ordered by; omit for no upper bound. Only with window LIFETIME.

preview_strategy_report.description: The many-coins-in-one-call market read: one table per report module with COINS AS ROWS, the schema preamble emitted once rather than per coin. Renders a bounded live-market preview of `source` over a required bounded `coinSelection`: either the report's own fields ({"kind":"FIELDS", timeframe, sections, conditions?, marketReadText?, marketReadLensTicker?}) or the player's strategy draft by reference ({"kind":"DRAFT", strategyId, draftVersion} at the draftVersion get_strategy_draft returned, composed exactly as its commit would compose it — a moved draft is refused with DRAFT_VERSION_MOVED). `detail` is "concise" (the default — exactly what the agent receives: each section's JSON, the grid and trade conditions blocks, marker statuses) or "detailed" (adds `authoring`: the condition column contract, every coin's full evaluation, and each rendered header's authored column). It returns server-owned budget usage — including `resultChars`, the exact characters of this result against the character cap it is refused over — without saving or mutating strategy state. A refusal over the character cap or the deadline carries `nextAct: "narrow"`: preview again asking for less — `detail: "concise"` unless you need `authoring`, otherwise fewer coins. Callable without the authoring vocabulary: a whole platform module is {"kind":"platform","sectionKey":"includeRsi"} (list them with list_strategy_categories), and {"mode":"ranked","limit":N} selects a cohort without naming coins — the top N by 24h volume, or by a ranked metric with {"rankBy":{"metric","ordering"}} (the leaders or laggards on that metric, each with its rows), within `category` (crypto when omitted, `ALL` for every asset class). Prefer this over looping a per-coin tool. The result describes the report you composed, not the platform catalog: `conditionColumns` carries the sections this report renders, while vocabulary that depends on no draft — a report-level scalar's gloss, operators and label vocabulary — is served by list_strategy_vocabulary and referenced here by `vocabularyDigest`, so resolve it once and cache it against that string. The preview execution limits (result character cap, deadline) are served by discovery as `previewExecutionLimits`.

rankBy.description: Order the ranked cohort by a ranked metric instead of 24h volume: `metric` is one whose `rankScope` is `exchangeWide` with served `rankOrderings` (list_strategy_vocabulary), and `ordering` one of those orderings. Ranked at the preview's own timeframe, within `category` (crypto when omitted; name `ALL` for every asset class), skipping a coin the ranked set does not hold.

bars.description: A column's `bars` names the bar set its values were read from: `Confirmed` — Read the newest bar that had COMPLETED at your strategy’s close. On the live report a value measured against the price — a distance, a moving-average alignment, a price zone — moves with the live price. At or below your strategy timeframe the two frames disagree, so this states both: on the live report it DROPS the bar in progress and changes the value read; at your strategy’s close no bar is in progress, so there it reads what the column reads anyway. A metric with no live value reads completed bars on both. `Developing` — Admit the higher-timeframe bar still in progress at your strategy’s close. It REPAINTS until that bar completes. A metric with no live value always reads completed bars, whatever this is set to. At or below your strategy timeframe the two frames disagree: on the live report it admits the bar in progress and repaints; at your strategy’s close no bar is in progress to admit, so there it reads what Confirmed reads. A metric with no live value has no bar in progress to admit on either, and reads completed bars.

spanFragments.description:
Define what each of the column's headers measures; they state neither its bar set, which `bars` carries, nor its bar position. A header ending `_dev` belongs to a column its author stored Developing; the header keeps it whatever bar set the column reads. A header ending `_o` reads the value N bars before the newest bar its read admits. A swing code followed by `_lr` reads swing pivots decided at L bars before and R closed bars after each pivot; a swing code without it reads the registered pair its gloss states. A market-structure code followed by `_s` reads the structure at a swing length of N, `_cf` with the confluence filter on, `_e` equal extremes at M bars and `_atr` within T × ATR; without them the defaults its gloss states. A structure-zone code followed by `_close` reads zones used up by a close past their far edge, computed by the server; without it, by a wick past it. An oscillator code followed by `_p` reads that oscillator over N bars; without it the registered length its code states. A stochastic header writes every setting once any is off its registered value: `_rsi` is the Stoch RSI's RSI length, `_p` the stochastic length, then `s` the %K smoothing and `d` the %D smoothing; a stochastic code without them reads the registered settings its gloss states. A MACD or PPO code followed by `_fastslowsig` reads it over F- and S-period close EMAs with a G-period signal; without it the registered settings its gloss states. A Bollinger code followed by `_psd` reads the bands over N closes at K standard deviations, and a Keltner code followed by `_patrmult` reads the channel at an N-period EMA ± M × the A-period ATR; without them the registered settings its gloss states. A Supertrend code followed by `_atrmult` reads the stop at M × the A-period ATR, and a Parabolic SAR code followed by `_startincmax` reads the SAR with acceleration starting at S, stepping by I and capped at X; without them the registered settings its gloss states. An Ichimoku code followed by `_convbasespanBdisp` reads the cloud with C-, B- and S-bar conversion, base and span B windows, the spans and the lagging close D − 1 bars back; without them the registered settings its gloss states. A supply/demand code followed by `_vt

` reads the zones at a P% volume threshold, and by `res` (after `_` when it opens the suffix) over N bins; without them LuxAlgo's defaults its gloss states.

get_strategy.description: Get one active visible strategy by default, with its complete report, entry conditions, trade-level policy (the ATR floor among it), lifecycle state, usage counts, and current revision. Set includeInactive:true to also reach your own strategies in any state, including an archived one being restored; the PRIVATE strategies of other users stay hidden either way.
